stimulus_db: Soaking dried beans overnight before cooking them reduces cooking time. However, cooking without presoaking yields plumper beans. Therefore, when a bean dish's quality is more important than the need to cook that dish quickly, beans should not be presoaked.
stem_db: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument?

choices_db.A: Plumper beans enhance the quality of a dish.
choices_db.B: There are no dishes whose quality improves with faster cooking.
choices_db.C: A dish's appearance is as important as its taste.
choices_db.D: None of the other ingredients in the dish need to be presoaked.
choices_db.E: The plumper the bean, the better it tastes.

steps.label: Evidence
steps.body:
Soaking dried beans overnight before cooking them reduces cooking time.
However, cooking without presoaking yields plumper beans.

steps.label: Conclusion
steps.body: Therefore, when a bean dish's quality is more important than the need to cook that dish quickly, beans should not be presoaked.

steps.label: Evaluate
steps.body: The argument assumes that plumper beans enhance the quality of the dish.

notes.body: This bridges the gap between plumper beans and a higher quality dish.
B is too strong. The argument can allow that some dishes do better with faster cooking. It only says that when a bean dish's quality matters more than speed, the beans shouldn't be presoaked.
The argument never compares appearance with taste. Plumper beans could improve a dish for any reason, so the argument doesn't need appearance to be as important as taste.
The argument is only about whether to presoak the beans. It needs no claim about whether anything else in the dish gets presoaked.

E links plumpness to taste, but the conclusion is about a dish's quality. The argument doesn't need plumpness to work through taste: plumper beans could improve a dish's quality even if they taste no better.

known_problem: One-line notes, no negation test on a Necessary Assumption; typo "This fail to connect".
